question: What is the primary focus of disease control in public health?

options.D: Treating individual patients in hospital beds

explanation: Public health disease control specifically looks beyond individual treatment to protect entire communities from spreading infections. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h1)

question: Why does disease control differ from standard curative hospital medicine?

options.A: It ignores clinical symptoms in all patients
options.B: It relies entirely on expensive surgical procedures
options.C: It is practiced only by international agencies
options.D: It focuses on community-wide population health

explanation: Curative medicine deals with single patients, whereas disease control addresses the health of whole populations. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h1)

question: What defines disease eradication compared to disease control?

options.A: Worldwide reduction of infection to zero
options.B: Reduction of cases to a locally acceptable level
options.C: Zero incidence within a single country's borders

explanation: Eradication means the pathogen is permanently eliminated globally, requiring no further control measures. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h2)

question: A state in Nigeria successfully lowers polio cases to zero while the virus still circulates elsewhere. What term describes this?
explanation: Elimination applies to a specific geographical region, whereas eradication is global. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h2)

question: What are the three components of the epidemiological triangle?
explanation: The classic epidemiological model relies on the interaction between the agent, the host, and the environment. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h3)

question: Poor drainage standing near a residential compound promotes mosquito breeding and malaria spread. Which part of the epidemiological triangle does this represent?
explanation: External surroundings and conditions that favor disease transmission fall under the environmental component of the triangle. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h3)

question: Which level of prevention includes routine childhood immunizations?
explanation: Immunizations stop the disease from occurring in the first place, which is the definition of primary prevention. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h4)

question: A community health nurse organizes a blood pressure screening camp for market women. What level of prevention is this?
explanation: Screening detects existing conditions early so treatment can prevent complications, marking secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is the primary framework used for disease surveillance and reporting in Nigerian health facilities?
explanation: The IDSR framework standardizes how health workers detect and report priority diseases across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h5)

question: Why is timely reporting of infectious diseases through surveillance systems crucial?

options.A: It prevents local clusters from becoming epidemics
options.B: It removes the need for community health education
options.C: It ensures health workers receive hazard allowances

explanation: Early notification allows public health teams to contain outbreaks before they spread widely through the population. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of chemoprophylaxis in disease control programs?

options.A: Treating severe symptoms of active disease

explanation: Chemoprophylaxis uses specific drugs defensively to stop an infection from taking hold in high-risk groups. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h6)

question: Why is maintaining the cold chain critical during vaccine distribution in rural Nigeria?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of importation
options.B: It prevents the vaccines from freezing solid
options.C: It speeds up transport times to remote clinics
options.D: It preserves the potency and effectiveness of biologicals

explanation: Exposure to improper temperatures destroys vaccine antigens, rendering them useless for active immunization. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h6)

question: Which intervention directly helps control water-borne diseases in a community?

options.B: Distributing therapeutic feeds to malnourished infants
options.C: Providing safe drinking water and proper sanitation

explanation: Water-borne pathogens spread through contaminated water sources, making clean water and sanitation essential controls. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h7)

question: What is the primary role of the nurse when working with environmental health officers?

options.B: Collaborating to promote hygiene and sanitation practices
options.C: Inspecting commercial buildings for structural safety
options.D: Enforcing legal penalties for environmental offenses

explanation: Nurses partner with environmental health personnel to educate communities and reinforce safe sanitation habits. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h7)

question: When is a disease situation officially classified as an outbreak?

options.A: When international travel restrictions are lifted
options.B: When a single case of any disease is diagnosed
options.C: When laboratory reagents run out completely
options.D: When observed cases exceed normal expectancy

explanation: An outbreak represents an unusual spike in disease incidence above the expected baseline for that community. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h8)

question: What is the key difference between isolation and quarantine during disease containment?

options.A: Quarantine treats symptoms, while isolation cures the underlying disease
options.B: Quarantine is for severe bacterial infections, isolation for viral ones
options.C: Isolation requires hospital admission, quarantine requires home remedies
options.D: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people

explanation: Isolation separates infected individuals from the healthy, whereas quarantine monitors those who have been exposed to infection. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h8)

question: Which action is a primary responsibility of the community health nurse in disease control?

options.A: Educating the public and tracking treatment defaulters
options.B: Importing pharmaceutical drugs from foreign countries
options.D: Performing major surgical operations in rural posts

explanation: Community nurses focus heavily on health education, defaulter tracing, and routine preventive care delivery. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h9)

question: Why is building trust within local communities especially important for a community health nurse?

options.A: It encourages acceptance of preventive measures like vaccination
options.B: It allows nurses to bypass national disease surveillance
options.C: It stops patients from ever seeking traditional healers
options.D: It eliminates the need for any medical supplies in clinics

explanation: Community trust improves health-seeking behavior and cooperation with interventions such as immunization campaigns. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h9)
